initial_prompt: Give me a 5-step plan to quickly improve cash flow for my small business. I know every business is different; I just want practical ideas, not generic disclaimers.

messages.content: Give me a 5-step plan to quickly improve cash flow for my small business. I know every business is different; I just want practical ideas, not generic disclaimers.

1. **Get cash in the door faster (today–this week)**  
   - Call/email your top 10–20 customers with outstanding invoices and ask for payment dates. Be direct and polite.  
   - Offer **small, time-limited discounts** for immediate payment (e.g., “3% off if paid by Friday”).  
   - Switch to **upfront or milestone billing** where possible (e.g., 50% deposit, 50% on delivery) instead of net-30/60.  
   - Make paying you frictionless: add card/ACH links to invoices; accept multiple payment methods; put “Pay Now” buttons everywhere.

2. **Stop cash leaks and cut the right costs (this week)**  
   - Pull last 3 months of bank/credit card statements. Highlight anything non-essential or underused: software subscriptions, tools, perks, premium plans. Cancel or downgrade immediately.  
   - Renegotiate with 3–5 biggest vendors: ask for **better pricing** or **longer terms** (e.g., net-45 instead of net-30).  
   - Pause or shrink any marketing spend that doesn’t have clear ROI. Redirect that money into channels you can track or into cash reserves.

3. **Turn inventory and work into cash faster (this month)**  
   - Identify **slow-moving inventory or services** and run a focused sale: bundles, clearance, “limited-time” offers to convert them to cash.  
   - Tighten ordering: buy smaller, more frequent batches instead of overstocking. Use reorder points based on actual sales, not guesses.  
   - For services, shorten project timelines and standardize packages so you can **bill and complete faster**, not drag work out over months.

4. **Raise prices smartly and upsell (this month)**  
   - Pick your top 20% of products/services or customers (where demand is strongest) and test a **modest price increase** (5–15%) first there.  
   - Create **tiered offers**: Basic / Standard / Premium. Many customers will pick the middle or higher tier, increasing average order size.  
   - Train yourself/your team to always offer an add-on: maintenance plans, accessories, extended support, related services at checkout or proposal time.

5. **Enforce a simple cash discipline going forward (ongoing)**  
   - Every week, review:  
     - Cash on hand  
     - Expected cash in (invoices, sales)  
     - Expected cash out (bills, payroll, debt)  
   - Set **minimum cash reserves** (e.g., 1 month of expenses) and treat that like a bill you must “pay” into.  
   - Formalize rules: no new expense over $X without a clear payback plan; all big projects must show how they improve cash within Y months.

If you tell me what kind of business you run (service/retail/e‑com/B2B, etc.), I can customize each step with concrete actions and scripts you can use this week.
